reason: The text explicitly contains God's (Yahweh's) declaration of His intention to help the Hebrew people. Specifically, God states: 'I have surely seen the affliction of my people which are in Egypt, and have heard their cry by reason of their taskmasters; for I know their sorrows; And I am come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians, and to bring them up out of that land unto a good land and a large, unto a land flowing with milk and honey.' This passage directly demonstrates that one of Yahweh's core goals is to help (specifically, to deliver and rescue) the Hebrew people from oppression and bring them to prosperity.
